CoreDNS v1.4.0 resolver flaw: a forged DNS response against the source port of CoreDNS's resolver. coredns is only an indirect dependency (go.mod) and juicefs starts no CoreDNS resolver or server. Checked: the driver (v0.34.0 pkg/, cmd/) runs only 'juicefs' subcommands format, status, config, quota set, rmr and version from /usr/local/bin/juicefs; none of cmd/format.go, status.go, config.go, quota.go, rmr.go, version.go starts a server, and the only listener in juicefs cmd/main.go is a debug agent on 127.0.0.1:6060+. Checked at juicefs commit 23d2a456, the last main commit before the image was created (2026-11-20; the Dockerfile builds juicefs from main). The govulncheck result for usr/local/bin/juicefs (digest sha256:1b5e3667) lists the symbol as linked only as a dependency of the binary, so the code is present but no entry path runs it.

CVE-2023-6879 in libaom3 3.6.0-1+deb12u3: Increasing the resolution of video frames, while performing a multi-threaded encode, can result in a heap overflow in av1_loop_restoration_dealloc(). Evidence read with image-files from the pinned image (sha256:1b5e3667). Programs the driver runs and what they link (ELF DT_NEEDED): juicefs-csi-driver and jfsmount are static; /usr/local/bin/juicefs links libfdb_c (foundationdb-clients), librados2 and libgfapi0; mount, umount, findmnt, bash, dash, rm, cp and tini link only libc, libmount, libblkid, libsmartcols, libudev, libselinux, libacl, libattr and libtinfo; the startup Python 3.9 script loads libssl3 and zlib1g (_ssl, _hashlib, zlib). The Depends closure of those packages in /var/lib/dpkg/status has 73 of 315 packages and does not contain libaom3. The driver's exec calls are juicefs, mount/umount, rm, sh and bash (source grep of cmd/ and pkg/ at v0.34.0, including mount-utils), plus the startup juicefs script. The package is installed but no process in the pod loads or runs it.

setuptools package_index download functions allow code injection: needs setuptools to download packages, which nothing in the image does at run time. Checked on the pinned image (sha256:1b5e3667, read with image-files): the only Python the driver runs is /usr/bin/juicefs 'version' at startup (cmd/main.go:141). That script imports only the standard library (datetime, gzip, io, optparse, os, platform, re, subprocess, sys, syslog, threading, time, types, urllib, http.client, email.utils, functools) and nothing named in this finding. pip and setuptools belong to the slim base's Python 3.9; the script imports neither, nothing in the driver runs pip, and distutils-precedence.pth only loads the distutils shim, not the vulnerable code.

Needs curl/libcurl to open an sftp or scp (SSH) connection with a schemeless URL.
